_comment: Fit Finder data — ONE source for /fit/. Every feature line is lifted from src/_data/verticals.json (the Blueprint-checked, literally-true copy of the 12 vertical pages). RULES: no pricing, no invented stats, proof only where it really exists (proof: null renders NOTHING). Adding a profession = adding an entry here. Spec of record: vault page '406 Front Desk — Fit Finder (Public Vertical Tool Spec)'.

professions.label: Barbershops
pains: The mid-cut call rings out — and that client books down the street.
Instagram and Facebook DMs stack up all day and get answered at close, if at all.
Hours, prices, walk-ins, who's working Saturday — the same five questions, a thousand times.

features.body: A call you can't take instantly becomes a text conversation: "Sorry we missed you — want to grab a time?"
Hours, prices, location, each barber's schedule — answered instantly and accurately, any hour.
Clients get sent directly to your real booking page — even the right link for the barber they asked for.
Every DM answered in minutes with real info and a booking link — not left on read until close.
Anything the AI shouldn't handle gets flagged to your phone with a summary — you jump in when it matters.

proof.text: This exact setup runs right now in a real Kalispell barbershop — the phone line, the texts, the Instagram and Facebook messages, and the website chat.

professions.label: Salons, Spas & Massage
pains: A colour service runs two hours — you physically cannot take that call.
"How much for balayage?" can't be quoted blind without undercharging or scaring off a booking.
The gift-card call always arrives mid-service, and somebody still has to answer it.

features.body: A call you couldn't take mid-service becomes a text conversation in seconds, instead of a voicemail you clear at close.
Services, rough timings, what's included, gift cards, parking, whether you take walk-ins — answered instantly and accurately, any hour.
Colour, extensions and corrections get captured — length, current colour, what they're after — then handed to you. It only quotes what you've published.
When a slot opens, it offers it out and takes the first yes, so a late cancellation doesn't become a dead two hours.
A nudge when a client is due, so the six-week colour cycle doesn't quietly stretch to ten and the monthly massage doesn't lapse.

professions.label: Tattoo & Piercing
pains: You're gloved up for four hours and every inquiry waits until you're done — the ones who wanted an answer today are already messaging the next artist.
Most DMs arrive with no size, no placement and no reference — answering properly means asking the same four questions over and over.
"How much for a sleeve?" is unanswerable without seeing it, and answering badly costs you the piece or the trust.

features.strong: Works the DMs, not just the phone
features.body: Instagram and Facebook messages answered in minutes — the channels most studios actually run on, and the ones that go unread longest.
The idea, rough size, placement, colour or black-and-grey, references, budget range and timeline — gathered before it ever reaches you.
It explains how you price and what a consult involves, then tells them you'll confirm. No number goes out that you didn't set.
Deposits, shop minimum policy, age and ID, hours, parking, walk-ins versus appointment, whether you're booking at all right now.
Start with capture only. Once you trust it, let it put fixed-length consultations straight onto a calendar.

professions.label: Pet Grooming, Boarding & Vets
pains: You're holding a wet, wriggling dog — the phone rings out and the caller books with whoever picks up first.
Everyone calls about holiday boarding in the same two weeks; whoever answers fills the kennel.
"How much for a groom?" depends on breed, coat and matting — quote it blind and you've lost money or lost the client.

features.body: A call you couldn't take mid-groom becomes a text conversation, instead of a voicemail you clear after closing.
Breed, size, coat condition, age, temperament, and what the owner is actually asking for — captured before you call back.
It explains how you price and what changes it — matting, size, coat type — then tells them you'll confirm. No number goes out that you didn't set.
The single most repeated question in boarding and daycare, answered instantly from the policy you've published.
New appointments onto your calendar, and a nudge when a regular is due for their next groom, so the six-week cycle doesn't quietly become twelve.

professions.label: Clinics & Health Practices
pains: A new patient calls while your desk is checking someone in — it rings out, and they book with the next practice that picks up.
People look for care in the evening and on weekends, when your desk is closed. Voicemail loses them.
Hours, location, what you treat, whether you take new patients — the same intake questions, all day.

features.body: A call you can't take instantly becomes a text: "Sorry we missed you — want to get you scheduled?"
Hours, location, what you treat, new-patient availability, how to book — answered instantly and accurately, any hour.
New patients get sent to your real booking page for a consult or appointment — no phone tag, no double-booking.
Inquiries that don't book right away get a gentle, automatic nudge so they don't slip through the cracks.
Anything clinical or sensitive is flagged to your staff with a summary. The AI never gives medical advice, and it never touches a health record.

proof.text: A Flathead clinic runs on this system today — Kalispell TRT's calls, texts, chat and telehealth booking all go through their 406 front desk.

professions.label: Chiropractors
pains: "I threw my back out" doesn't shop around — whoever answers first gets the patient.
A care plan is two or three visits a week, and every change is a phone call.
"Do you take my insurance?" deserves a straight answer at 8 PM, not a voicemail.

features.body: A call nobody could reach becomes a text conversation in seconds, instead of a voicemail your desk works through after close.
It tells callers which plans you're in-network with and what a cash visit runs, then hands anything specific to your team. It never verifies benefits or promises coverage.
New-patient calls go straight onto the schedule instead of into a callback pile — including the ones that come in at 9 PM.
The "can I move Thursday?" message gets handled without anyone picking up a phone, so care plans stay intact.
Anything clinical, anything sensitive, anything unusual goes to your staff with a summary of the conversation.

professions.label: Dental Practices
pains: Plenty of practices are dark three days a week — a broken tooth on a Saturday goes to whoever answers.
Hygiene recall is the most valuable list in the practice and the first thing that slips when the desk is busy.
Someone cancels an hour out and the chair sits empty while nobody at the desk has a free minute to fill it.

features.body: A call nobody could reach becomes a text conversation in seconds, including on the days and hours the office is closed.
It recognises urgency, gives your posted after-hours instructions, and gets the patient onto the first available slot. It never assesses the problem.
Overdue patients get a friendly text that books them, instead of a call your desk never gets to. The list finally gets worked.
When a slot opens, it offers it out and takes the first yes — so the chair gets filled without anyone dialling down a list.
Anything clinical, anything about a specific treatment plan, anything sensitive goes to your team with a summary of the conversation.

professions.label: Physical Therapy
pains: A physician sends a referral and nobody reaches them for two days — they call the next clinic, and the referring office notices.
Patients start a plan of care strong and fade — every skipped visit is worse outcomes for them and lost revenue for you.
A move or a second location brings a call surge exactly when your front desk is least able to absorb it.

features.body: A call your desk couldn't reach becomes a text conversation in seconds, instead of a voicemail cleared at the end of the day.
New patients get scheduled the same day they call rather than waiting on a callback — the single biggest reason referrals leak to another clinic.
Whether a referral is needed, what to bring, what the first visit involves, how long sessions run — answered from what you've published, any hour.
Reminders and easy rescheduling by text, so a missed visit becomes a moved visit instead of the moment someone quietly stops coming.
When a slot opens, it offers it out and takes the first yes — so a late cancellation doesn't leave a therapist idle.

professions.label: Gyms & Fitness Studios
pains: You're spotting a set or running the floor — the membership call rings out and they join the gym that picked up.
People decide to get in shape at night, on the couch — hours before anyone's at your desk.
Every Instagram message sitting on read is someone who was ready to walk in this week.

features.body: A call you can't take instantly becomes a text conversation: "Sorry we missed you — want to come take a look?"
Rates, hours, day passes, class times, childcare, what's included, how contracts work — answered instantly, any hour.
Prospects get put straight onto your real calendar for a walkthrough, a free week, or a first session.
Every DM answered in minutes with real info and a booking link — not left until someone gets to the office.
A chat bubble on your site that answers questions and captures the prospect's name and number before they bounce.

professions.label: Trades & Contractors
pains: You're in a crawlspace, on a roof, or elbow-deep in a panel — the caller dials the next name on the list.
A furnace dies at midnight in January. Whoever answers first gets the job, and usually the bigger repair that follows it.
Half your calls are people pricing a job they may never book, and sorting them out costs the same interruption either way.

features.body: A call you can't take on the job becomes a text conversation instead of a voicemail you hear at dinner.
What's the problem, where's the property, how urgent, owner or renter — captured before it reaches you, so you know if it's worth a truck roll.
Real jobs go straight onto your calendar as estimate appointments — not into a voicemail queue you work through at 8 PM.
A no-heat call in January isn't a Tuesday quote request. Urgent jobs get flagged and routed to you or your on-call right away.
Anything that needs a tradesman's answer — scope, price, code questions — goes to you with a summary of the conversation.

professions.label: Auto Shops
pains: You're on a lift or halfway through an install — the phone rolls to voicemail and the caller tries the next shop.
"How much for…" arrives before they've told you the vehicle, and sorting it out costs the same interruption either way.
People look for a shop after work and on Sunday afternoon, when the bay is dark.

features.body: A call you can't take from under a car becomes a text conversation instead of a voicemail you clear at closing.
Year, make, model, and what's actually wrong — captured before it reaches you, so the callback doesn't start from zero.
Real jobs go onto your calendar as drop-offs or estimate appointments, not into a voicemail queue you work through after close.
It captures what the job involves and tells the customer you'll confirm the price. No number goes out that you didn't set.
Anything that needs your judgment — a diagnosis, an odd vehicle, a scope question — comes to you with a summary of the conversation.

professions.label: CPAs & Accounting
pains: February through April the phone doesn't stop, and every minute on it is a minute not spent on a return.
"Is my return done yet?" — the same status check, twenty times a week.
A business owner shopping for a new accountant in July calls three firms. The one that picks up gets a client worth years.

features.body: A call you can't take becomes a text conversation instead of a voicemail you'll return at nine tonight.
Hours, location, what you charge to prepare, what to bring, deadlines and extension dates — answered instantly, any hour.
Individual or business, entity type, which services, roughly what scale — captured before the call reaches you, so you know if it's a fit.
Qualified prospects go straight onto your calendar for an intro call — not into a queue you work through on Sunday.
Automatic follow-ups to the clients still sitting on their W-2s, 1099s, or signed engagement letter.

fallback.label: Your business
fallback.intro: We don't have a page for your exact line of work yet — but if the phone rings while your hands are busy, the core system fits. Here's what every 406 front desk does, whatever the trade:

features.body: A call you can't take instantly becomes a text conversation instead of a voicemail — the conversation continues instead of dying.
Hours, location, what you do, how to get started — answered instantly and accurately, any hour, on every channel.
Real inquiries go straight onto the calendar you already keep — no migration, no double-booking.

features.strong: Follows up with the quiet ones
features.body: Leads that don't book right away get a gentle, automatic nudge so they don't slip through the cracks.
Anything that needs your judgment lands on your phone with a summary of the conversation so far.

fallback.note: Every line above is a feature we already deploy — nothing here is hypothetical. Tell us what you do on a twenty-minute call and we'll map it to your business specifically.
